findings.text: Idle-group comparison is ordered first by group classification rank, with a lower rank always displacing the current best and a higher rank never doing so. When ranks tie, overloaded and fully busy groups prefer smaller average load, misfit groups prefer larger maximum capacity, groups with spare prefer more idle CPUs then smaller utilization, while balance and packing related classes never displace in this path.

Group cookie compatibility has two build variants. Without core scheduling support it is unconditionally compatible. With support it remains compatible when core scheduling is disabled on the local runqueue, otherwise it is compatible when at least one CPU shared between the group span and the task affinity has a matching cookie.

CPU cookie compatibility is unconditionally true without core scheduling support or when that facility is disabled on the examined runqueue; otherwise compatibility means equality between the runqueue core cookie and the task core cookie.
The single-CPU idle probe succeeds only when both idle eligibility and cookie compatibility hold, returning the probed CPU on success and a negative sentinel meaning none otherwise.
There is a static branch key recording whether symmetric multithreading is present in the system.

Idle-core hints are maintained under read-side RCU protection. The updater observes the per-CPU shared balance object and, when present, publishes the hint with a single atomic-sized store. Promotion to idle-core state scans every sibling in the SMT mask and publishes only when all other siblings are available idle, while holding an RCU read lock across the whole check.

Core-level probing examines all hardware threads of one core, remembers the first affinity-allowed idle thread as a fallback candidate, and reports the core itself only when every thread is available idle; otherwise it removes the entire core mask from further consideration.
SMT sibling search stays within the intersection of the target core mask, task affinity and last-level-cache domain span, skips the target itself, and returns the first idle-eligible sibling or none.

General idle-CPU scan is bounded by a shared idle-scan hint when the utilization-aware search feature is active, aborting early when the domain appears overloaded, and is restricted to the intersection of domain span and task affinity. Cluster systems first probe the local cluster group, then wrap around from after the target; the idle-core path delegates per-core while the plain path consumes the scan budget per CPU, and a stale idle-core hint is cleared when core preference was active.

Asymmetric fit ranks are ordered integers with misfit on idle core at minus four, complete misfit at minus three, thread fits at minus two, thread uclamp misfit at minus one, thread misfit at zero, and idle-core bias at minus three.

Capacity-aware idle search prefers a thread whose utilization and clamps fully fit and which sits on a preferred fully-idle core, returning immediately in that case. Otherwise candidates are ranked by fit level shifted to favor preferred cores, breaking ties toward larger capacity, with scan budget applied only when no idle core is advertised and with the idle-core hint cleared when the winner is not on an idle core.

Asymmetric admission is always true on symmetric capacity systems; on asymmetric systems it requires full utilization and clamp fit and additionally requires an idle core when multithreading is active.

This wakeup placement entry expects interrupts disabled and consults cached utilization when asymmetry is active. It considers the target, cache-affine previous CPU, per-CPU kthread stacking, and recently used CPU with cluster sharing checks, then takes either an asymmetric capacity domain path or a last-level-cache path with SMT and general scans, finally falling back to preserved affine candidates or the target while recording the previous CPU as recent.
A task counts as a per-CPU kernel thread exactly when it carries the kernel-thread flag and is allowed on a single CPU.
An externally visible helper reports the effective utilization of a named CPU.
The energy estimation context carries four unsigned capacity-time quantities: task busy time, performance-domain busy time, per-CPU capacity, and aggregated domain capacity.
Per-task busy time is derived from the task estimated utilization scaled down by interrupt pressure observed on the previous CPU, saturated at that CPU maximum capacity.
Domain busy time is the sum over domain CPUs of their effective utilization, saturated at the domain capacity.

Domain peak requirement is the maximum over domain CPUs of clamp-aware effective performance, incorporating runqueue and task clamp bounds with distinct handling for idle versus busy runqueues, saturated at per-CPU capacity.

Energy for a placement adds the task busy contribution to domain busy time when a destination is evaluated, delegates to the CPU energy model with peak and busy inputs, and emits a trace record of the inputs and result.

Energy-aware placement returns none when performance domains are absent or when no asymmetric domain covers both local and previous CPUs, defaults to the previous CPU, and bypasses search for zero-estimate tasks without minimum clamp. Otherwise it walks performance domains restricted to online CPUs, tracks previous-CPU and best-spare candidates by fit level then spare capacity, and compares incremental energy deltas against a domain baseline, aborting to the previous CPU when utilization changed concurrently. Only the first part of this routine is visible here.
Runqueue idleness for clamping has two build variants: one reports the idle flag bit, the other reports never idle.

Placement relies on per-CPU scratch masks and RCU-protected domain pointers that require disabled interrupts and RCU read protection respectively; energy deltas assume stable utilization across baseline and candidate evaluation, and a decrease indicates a race and forces fallback rather than trusting the comparison.
Wakeup placement requires interrupts disabled on entry, asserted at runtime.

The per-domain idle-core hint transitions to set only after observing all SMT siblings idle, remains set until a capacity or general scan runs with core preference active but selects a non-idle-core or no core, at which point it transitions back to clear.
